landmarks.name: Caloris Planitia
landmarks.origin: "Hot plain"; surface temperature hottest near this position.

quote.text: Very large impact basins, including Caloris (960 miles or 1,550 kilometers in diameter) and Rachmaninoff (190 miles, or 306 kilometers in diameter), were created by asteroid impacts on the planet's surface early in the solar system's history.

landmarks.name: Rachmaninoff
landmarks.origin: Sergei V.; Russian composer, pianist, and conductor (1873-1943).

quote.text: Whereas pre-MESSENGER interpretations were that volcanism on Mercury ended early in the planet's history, MESSENGER's images of Rachmaninoff reveal that some volcanism extended well beyond that time, probably into the second half of Solar System history.

landmarks.name: Borealis Planitia
landmarks.origin: "Northern plain"; from classical albedo name for quadrangle.

quote.text: The vast plains surrounding Mendelssohn, called Borealis Planitia, were formed by the widespread eruption of runny lava some 3.7 billion years ago.

landmarks.name: Caloris Montes
landmarks.origin: "Hot mountains"; surface temperature hottest near this position.

quote.text: The floor of the Caloris basin is filled with volcanic plains , while the Caloris Montes , a ring of mountainous peaks, are found along the basin's rim.

landmarks.name: Enterprise Rupes
landmarks.origin:
American; steamship that explored the Mississippi, Amazon, and
Madeira Rivers and sailed on a worldwide hydrographic survey 1877 to
1886.

quote.text: Enterprise Rupes, about 1000 km long and with over 3 km of relief, is the largest lobate scarp on Mercury!

landmarks.name: Rembrandt
landmarks.origin: Rembrandt Harmenszoon van Rijn; Dutch painter (1606-1669).

quote.text: The number per area and size distribution of impact craters superposed on Rembrandt's rim indicates that it is one of the youngest impact basins on Mercury.

landmarks.name: Beagle Rupes
landmarks.origin: British; naval vessel aboard which Charles Darwin served as a naturalist on a surveying expedition, 1831-1836.

quote.text: Beagle Rupes and other scarps on Mercury are thought to be the surface expressions of thrust faults that formed from contraction as the planet's interior cooled.

landmarks.name: Pantheon Fossae
landmarks.origin: Classic domed Roman building begun in 27 BC by Marcus Agrippa, and rebuilt by Hadrian between AD 118 and 128.

quote.text: The dome of the Pantheon has a series of sunken panels that radiate from a central circular opening at the top of the dome, and Mercury's Pantheon Fossae is reminiscent of this pattern.
The Mendelssohn crater was flooded with lava after an impact originally created it.

landmarks.name: Raditladi
landmarks.origin: Leetile Disang; Botswanan playwright and poet (1910-1971).

quote.text: Raditladi basin is relatively young, with only a few small impact craters on the basin's floor and with well-preserved basin walls and peak-ring structure.

landmarks.name: Hokusai
landmarks.origin: Katsushika; Japanese painter, draftsman, and printmaker (1760-1849).

quote.text: The crater has an impressive system of rays, which extend as much as a thousand kilometers (more than 600 miles) across the planet and are the longest that have yet been identified on Mercury.
MESSENGER has found evidence that within the cold, dark, permanently shadowed regions of Prokofiev, water ice is exposed on the surface.
The floor of Kandinsky is in permanent shadow and never receives direct sunlight, keeping it very cold.

landmarks.name: Apollodorus
landmarks.origin: Apollodorus of Damascus; Greek architect (2nd century AD).

quote.text: The crater Apollodorus near the center of Pantheon Fossae is 41 kilometers (25 miles) in diameter.
